title: The Balanced Books Challenge
details: All eleven Transaction Inbox events, ten Equation Lab transactions, first-pass scores, corrected running balances, statement totals, feedback, teaching explanations and three financial statements are retained. All transaction-prefix balances/equation components and final statements match independent Python oracles. Both legacy components are replaced by native DOM: the statement workspace uses isolated native styling, drag/drop, keyboard/touch placement, validation, reset, totals and original thinking prompts; page scrolling uses native browser APIs. No iframe, Streamlit bridge or Python runtime is loaded. Arrows traverse 26 meaningful positions, including the three separately earned statement pages. Future statement tabs stay blocked; earlier statements have no editing, checks, reset or new explanation controls. Completed-lesson review renders completed statements without mutation or hint controls. Browser tests cover actual mouse drag/drop, keyboard placement, wrong classifications/effects, wrong statement checks, partial placement/order across review and refresh, all three statements and honest first-pass scores.
compatibility: Original version-1 saved links import at /js/, including all 24 original lesson positions. Native version-2 snapshots retain the original fields while distinguishing the three statement positions, preserving larger practice counters, and recording viewed position separately from earned work. Legacy statement views are normalized only from valid finalized/work state; fabricated future statement work is rejected. Native links should be opened at /js/, because the original Python/root application does not accept version 2. Refresh and bookmarks retain answers, drafts, selected/placed tiles, randomized account order, validation attempts and review position. Thinking explanations stay session-only and close after refresh, matching the original design. No central saving or service is added.
